criteria.text: The participant is at least 18 years of age.
The participant has histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced solid tumors.

For Arm #1 (KO-2806 monotherapy), the participant has progressed on, or is refractory to, standard of care (SOC) treatments with advanced solid tumors, specifically: HRAS-mutant and/or amplified tumors (any solid tumor type); HRAS overexpression (only for HNSCC tumors); KRAS and/or NRAS, and/or HRAS-mutant and/or amplified NSCLC or CRC; KRAS-mutant and/or amplified PDAC.

For Arm #2 (Combination), the participant has received at least 1 prior systemic therapy with IO-based treatment for locally advanced or metastatic RCC with predominantly clear cell subtype; non-clear cell RCC patients who are either treatment-naïve or have received any prior systemic treatment for locally advanced and metastatic RCC.

For Arm #3 (Combination), the participant has received at least 1 prior systemic therapy including available approved SOC treatments for KRAS G12C-mutant locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, CRC, or PDAC.

For Arm #4 (Combination), the participant must be cabozantinib-naïve and have received at least 1 prior systemic therapy with IO-based treatment for locally advanced or metastatic ccRCC, but no more than 3 prior systemic anticancer therapies.

For Arm #5 (Cabozantinib monotherapy), the participant must be cabozantinib-naïve and have received at least 1 prior systemic therapy with IO-based treatment for locally advanced or metastatic ccRCC, but no more than 3 prior systemic anticancer therapies.

For Arm #6 (Cabozantinib rollover to combination), the participant must be cabozantinib-naïve and have received at least 1 prior systemic therapy with IO-based treatment for locally advanced or metastatic ccRCC, but no more than 3 prior systemic anticancer therapies.
For Arm #7 (Combination), the participant has received at least 1 prior systemic therapy including available approved SOC treatments for KRAS G12C-mutant locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC.
The participant has measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1.
The participant has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 70 or higher with no clinically significant deterioration over the previous 2 weeks.
The participant has acceptable liver, renal, endocrine, and hematologic function.
Other protocol-defined inclusion criteria may apply.
The participant has used any anticancer therapy within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) of Cycle 1 Day 1.
The participant has had prior treatment with an FTI or HRAS inhibitor.
The participant has had major surgery, other than local procedures, within 28 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1, without complete recovery.
The participant has spinal cord compression, leptomeningeal disease, or clinically active CNS metastases.
The participant has toxicity (excluding alopecia) from prior therapy that has not been completely resolved to baseline at the time of consent.
The participant has active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders within the past 5 years prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 (with exceptions).
The participant has active, uncontrolled bacterial, viral, or fungal infections requiring systemic therapy.
The participant has inability to swallow, impairment of gastrointestinal (GI) function or GI disease that may significantly alter the absorption of the trial drugs.

The participant has inadequate cardiac and/or vascular function, including receipt of treatment for unstable angina, myocardial infarction, and/or cerebrovascular attack within the prior 6 months, mean QTcF ≥470 ms, or Class II or greater congestive heart failure.
The participant has had another invasive malignancy within 2 years.
Other protocol-defined exclusion criteria may apply.

transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "KO-2806 Monotherapy and Combination Therapies in Advanced Solid Tumors". Your earlier answers already covered 6 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 82 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a biopsy or test that confirmed you have an advanced solid tumor?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, he had a biopsy. We know he has non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to his liver.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you previously received standard cancer treatments for your tumor, and did the cancer continue to grow or return after those treatments?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, he had carboplatin chemo and Keytruda, but they stopped the Keytruda because it gave him bad colitis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Did the cancer continue to grow or return after the carboplatin and Keytruda treatments?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if it grew back after the treatment. I don't know the details of how the cancer responded.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you know roughly how many different systemic cancer treatments (like chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) he has received in total so far?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: He's only had one treatment so far, the chemo and Keytruda together.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: To clarify, has he received any other systemic cancer treatments (like chemo, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) besides the one cycle of carboplatin and Keytruda?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he hasn't had any other treatments besides that one round of chemo and Keytruda.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, has he received any other systemic anticancer treatments (like chemo, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) besides the one round of carboplatin and Keytruda?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he hasn't had any other treatments besides that one round of chemo and Keytruda.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be precise, has he received any other cancer treatments (chemo, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) besides that single round of carboplatin and Keytruda? Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he hasn't had any other treatments besides that one round of chemo and Keytruda.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. For this specific arm, has he received at least one prior systemic therapy (like chemo, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) approved for KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC? Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if he has a KRAS G12C mutation. I'd have to ask his doctor about that specific test result.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have his recent blood tests shown that his liver, kidney, hormone, and blood cell levels are within normal ranges? Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about his recent blood test results. I'm not sure what his liver, kidney, or blood cell levels are showing right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has he received any cancer treatments in the last 14 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he hasn't had any cancer treatments in the last 14 days.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has he ever received treatment with an FTI or an HRAS inhibitor? These are specific types of targeted cancer therapies. Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what an FTI or an HRAS inhibitor is. I'd have to ask his doctor if he's had those specific treatments.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has he had any major surgery in the last 28 days? By major surgery, I mean procedures that required a hospital stay or general anesthesia, not minor local procedures. Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, he hasn't had any major surgery in the last 28 days.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since the last 14 days, have any side effects from his previous cancer treatments (other than hair loss) persisted or not fully returned to his normal baseline state? Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: He had bad colitis from the Keytruda, but he finished the prednisone last month. I'm not sure if he has any other side effects lingering right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, is he currently experiencing any ongoing side effects from his cancer treatments, other than hair loss, that haven't fully gone away? Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: He finished the prednisone for the colitis last month, so I don't know if he has any other side effects lingering right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has he had any diagnosed autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (like rheumatoid arthritis or lupus) in the last 5 years? Please let me know if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Does he have any trouble swallowing, or any stomach or intestinal conditions that might affect how his body absorbs medication?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if he has trouble swallowing or any stomach conditions that affect absorption. I'm not sure about that.
